jobs.description: 1、参与空间智能(含具身、智驾)大模型前沿算法研究,涵盖4D通用表征、多模态感知融合(视觉/触觉/力觉)、空间理解与推理、端到端运动规划、动作生成等模块的数据生成、算法开发、模型训练优化及评测迭代等工作,持续提升大模型空间智能竞争力。 2、开展细粒度4D空间对齐与推理技术研究,在VLM中引入4D空间特征编码网络并对齐到LLM语义空间,同时通过DiT/世界模型等技术提升模型的空间推理能力,实现对4D场景的精细化理解。 3、参与构建大模型的时空间理解与推理能力,实现快慢思考自适应切换,基于CoT压缩与推理加速、高质量CoT生成、强化微调等技术,在保持因果推理能力的同时降低时延,应用于自动驾驶与具身智能。 4、将业界先进VLA, VLN, World Model, Agent, 强化学习, 迁移学习等技术应用于自动驾驶、具身智能领域,实现安全高效的动作生成,提升自动驾驶在复杂场景下的推理、规划和决策能力,以及机器人各类应用的通用技能。 5、协同团队推动算法落地应用与技术竞争力构建:包括大规模数据采集与生成、Sim-to-Real迁移、真机部署等工作,搭建空间智能/具身智能技术平台,确保技术方案领先性与差异化;紧跟业界和学术界空间智能领域最新研究进展,参与业界顶会,将前沿成果融入研发。

Title: AI数据与仿真工程师(双休,需要有全职工作经验)招聘_西湖交互机器科技(杭州)有限公司招聘 - 智联招聘
# AI数据与仿真工程师(双休,需要有全职工作经验) 你的价值,本该更高. 1. 负责机器人及相关业务场景下时序数据、传感器数据与实验数据的全链路治理,完成数据清洗、特征挖掘、统计分析与可视化呈现,为AI算法迭代提供高质量数据支撑。. 2. 参与数据处理核心算法模块的研发落地,覆盖信号滤波、特征提取、异常检测、分类与回归预测等场景,解决多源异构数据的时间同步、对齐融合等技术问题。. 4. 基于Isaac Sim、MuJoCo等主流物理仿真平台,搭建高保真仿真环境与自动化测试工具链,完成仿真场景构建、批量数据生成与仿真结果校验。. 5. 负责数字资产生命周期管理,完成三维模型导入、格式转换、碰撞体设置及基础物理属性配置,保障仿真环境与真实场景的一致性。. 6. 配合算法团队完成数据分析模块、AI训练接口与仿真工具的功能联调、测试验证与问题排查,支撑具身智能算法的快速迭代与落地。. 1. 硕士及以上学历,计算机、人工智能、软件工程、自动化、电子信息等相关专业,欢迎优秀应届毕业生及具备相关项目经验的社会人才投递。. 2. 具备扎实的Python编程能力,能够独立完成数据处理脚本、分析模块及工具的开发工作;熟悉Linux系统基本操作,具备良好的软件调试与问题排查能力。. 3. 熟练使用NumPy、Pandas、Matplotlib等常用数据处理与可视化工具,掌握数据清洗、特征提取、统计分析及时序信号处理的常规方法。. 4. 了解机器学习/深度学习基础理论,熟悉PyTorch、Scikit-learn等框架的基本使用,有相关课程设计、科研项目或实际开发经验者优先。. 5. 对三维模型、数字资产及物理仿真技术有浓厚兴趣,了解USD、URDF、MJCF等常见资产格式,愿意长期深耕仿真工具与平台开发方向。. 6. 满足以下任一条件者优先考虑:有Isaac Sim、MuJoCo等仿真平台实际使用经验;有CAD、Mesh模型处理或数字资产整理经验;有时序数据、传感器数据或多源异构数据融合分析经验;有AI算法、仿真工具或数据分析相关落地项目经验。. ## articles.summary: World models enable embodied agents to anticipate action consequences, yet jointly modeling locomotion and manipulation across diverse embodiments remains challenging due to heterogeneous action spaces and limited multimodal supervision. articles.summary: Vision-and-language navigation (VLN) relies on retaining and using relevant observations. Yet growing histories introduce redundancy, and retained information may remain underused. articles.title: Learn the Task, Not the Schedule: Reducing Spurious Cross-Arm Coupling in Bimanual Imitation Learning
articles.summary: A bimanual demonstration specifies both what the robot should do and one particular schedule for when each arm should act. Standard imitation learning does not distinguish task-required cross-arm constraints from incidental scheduling choices, and may therefore exploit opposite-arm progress as a shortcut cue, creating spurious cross-arm coupling even where relative timing is irrelevant for the current task phase. We introduce Constraint-preserving Temporal Recombination (CTR), a training-time data intervention that preserves recorded arm-local sensorimotor content while retiming the corresponding segments to realize admissible schedules that preserve task-required cross-arm constraints. We use CTR to train Diffusion Policy, Action Chunking with Transformers, and $π_{0.5}$, and evaluate them on four simulated and four real-robot tasks. Across six real-robot bimanual progress-state initializations, CTR raises worst-state success from 56% for the strongest non-CTR schedule mixture to 76%.

articles.title: RoboMMT: Learning Stable Tracking of Modulated Expressive and Interactive Robot Motion
articles.summary: Expressive robot motion can improve naturalness, effectiveness, and perceived likability in human-robot interaction. When deployed on dynamically unstable platforms, however, reactive execution of expressive body motion may bring the robot to its stability limits, especially when expressivity is decoupled from physical control. Our approach trains a reference-conditioned tracking policy across a broad domain of expressivity, enabling it to faithfully realize the commanded motions while maintaining dynamic stability. articles.summary: Tactile perception is crucial for precise robotic manipulation, providing an important foundation for dexterous, closed-loop force control. articles.summary: Learning from Demonstration (LfD) allows robots to learn new skills from human examples; however, many vision-based methods require large datasets and resource-intensive end-to-end training. articles.summary: Fast and reliable manipulation is crucial for practical robot deployment. articles.title: CondenseVLA: Learnable History Condensation for Efficient Multi-Frame VLA
articles.summary: Robot manipulation often depends on short-term cues - such as brief contacts, temporary occlusions, and intermediate object states - that are ambiguous in a single frame and can only be resolved by integrating observations over time. However, injecting historical information solely by enlarging the history window is computationally costly and frequently yields limited gains due to substantial redundancy and task-agnostic, inflexible sampling of observations. Although world-action models (WAMs) improve control through future prediction, modeling complete future states wastes capacity on static appearance and action-irrelevant changes. articles.summary: Fine industrial robotic manipulation requires 6D pose, scale, and an operation-ready 3D model. articles.summary: Despite recent advances in policy learning, long-horizon manipulation remains difficult because learned policies must avoid compounding errors while preserving future feasibility. articles.summary: Experience generated during deployment offers an opportunity for robots to improve policy reliability through learning from their own executions. articles.summary: Humanoid robots operating in human-centric environments must coordinate the entire body to traverse tight, cluttered spaces while maintaining balance. articles.title: Validation of Human Motor Development Scales with Humanoid Robots
articles.summary: We investigate how humanoid robots can learn a series of motor skills defined by human infant motor development scales, and we evaluate which scales are comprehensive enough to serve as self-contained guides for developing gross motor skills up to standing and walking. We represent each motor development scale as a developmental graph that guides the training of a humanoid robot. We then apply this graph within a reinforcement learning framework so that the robot learns skills following the natural phases of human motor development described by the scale. Our work demonstrates that graphs derived from three out of four popular pediatric motor scales can successfully guide humanoid robots to develop these skills. articles.summary: Data-driven learning for general-purpose robotic manipulation presents a fundamental trade-off between data-collection cost and adaptability to real-world environments.
